top.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has rewarded each player and member of the technical crew of Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, with N10 million following their historic triumph at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. In addition to the cash reward, each player received an iPhone 18 Pro Max and bespoke outfits in recognition of the team’s achievement as the first African side to win the global tournament. Sanwo-Olu announced the reward package on Sunday evening while hosting the victorious squad to a special dinner reception at the Lagos House, Marina. The governor said the gesture was in recognition of the team’s landmark victory on the global stage, which has attracted widespread acclaim across Nigeria and the African continent. The reception provided an opportunity for the Lagos State Government to celebrate the players and technical crew for bringing honour to Nigeria and making history in women’s football. top.title: Sanusi, Ladoja warn against politicising traditional institutions
top.description: By Adeola Badru The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, and the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, have called for national healing, peaceful coexistence and stronger bonds among Nigeria’s diverse ethnic and religious groups, warning against the politicisation of traditional institutions. The two traditional rulers spoke on Sunday in Ibadan when Sanusi paid a courtesy visit to Ladoja at his palace in Oke-Aremo, where they stressed the need for traditional institutions to remain above partisan interests and serve as instruments of reconciliation, mutual understanding and national unity. Sanusi, who was in Ibadan to honour an invitation from the League of Imams and Alfas in South-West Nigeria, said his visit reflected his belief in a country where ethnic, religious and political differences would not determine relationships among citizens. He described the engagement as one of the positive developments needed to bridge Nigeria’s regional and cultural divides, stressing that national unity, progress and prosperity could only be achieved when people from different backgrounds deliberately reached out to one another. The Emir said although other engagements had emerged, he considered it important to honour his earlier commitment to attend the conference, even if his participation would be brief. “We fixed this date a long time ago, and even though other events came, we considered it important to honour our promise to appear at the conference, even if it is for a brief period, because they have been expecting me to come. “This invitation is part of the positive developments we have been yearning for to build a bridge where Nigerians from different parts of the country reach out to each other and come together in the interest of the unity, the progress and the prosperity of our dear nation,” he said. Sanusi also apologised for the delay in visiting Ladoja following his appointment and coronation, explaining that certain circumstances had prevented him from attending earlier. He congratulated Ladoja on his ascension to the throne of his forebears and prayed for divine protection, a long and peaceful reign, as well as prosperity for Ibadanland and Nigeria. The Emir described the courtesy visit as necessary, given the longstanding relationship between the two traditional institutions and their respective communities. He said Ibadan had remained a familiar destination over the years, adding that he had maintained close relationships with several indigenes of the city. top.title: NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers
top.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kwara, Prof. Abdulmumin Ajia, has pledged a minimum wage of N120,000 for workers in the state. Ajia made the pledge on Sunday in Ilorin while unveiling the NDC’s 2027 Gubernatorial Campaign Council manifesto, tagged ‘Forward Kwara Agenda’. He proposed a N120,000 public-service minimum wage benchmark and a cost-of-living adjustment framework for workers and pensioners. He said his administration would verify the payroll, assess the financial implications, consult labour unions and publish an implementation and funding timetable. On pensioners, Ajia promised to verify outstanding gratuities and publish a schedule for settling validated arrears. He also pledged to establish a predictable payment timetable for newly due pension obligations. Ajia said he entered the governorship race to make public institutions work reliably for all Kwarans, regardless of political affiliation. “I am running to make public institutions work that way. If entrusted with office, I will serve people who support me, people who oppose me and people who have never attended a political meeting,” he said. He said his experience as a teacher, researcher and university administrator had taught him to ask critical questions, examine evidence and take responsibility for results. Ajia, who led a School of Business and mentored young people, said his visits home exposed him to the challenges facing unemployed graduates. He said many young people could hardly predict when fair employment opportunities would become available. According to him, government has a responsibility to ensure that citizens understand how to access assistance, eligibility requirements and appeal procedures. He said access to public services should not depend on personal relationships with the governor. Ajia said the Forward Kwara Agenda outlined six areas of governance, anchored on stronger institutions, greater opportunities and shared prosperity. On security, he said farmers should access their farms, children should travel safely to school and traders should return home safely from markets. NAN reports that the event attracted hundreds of NDC stakeholders from the state’s 16 local government areas. top.title: ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach
top.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp praised Xavi Hernandez on Sunday, saying the new Netherlands coach already had the Dutch playing in his own image after just five games in charge. Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s meeting between the two old rivals, Klopp pointed to Friday’s 7-0 thumping of Greece in Amsterdam and said the former midfielder had made an impression. Considered among the best midfielders in the history of the game, Xavi formed the core of a possession-dominant Barcelona side who won four Champions League titles. He also won the World Cup with Spain. “They simply played some electric football,” Klopp said, adding: “Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football… “He’s a coach who really pushes his approach to the limit. And that’s exciting. I always loved playing against teams who play like this.” Third in the group with only the top two reaching the quarter-finals, Germany will need to beat the Netherlands to give themselves a chance. “They’re a team who really come alive in European football,” Klopp said of the Netherlands. “It’s one of the fiercest rivalries in football. It’s a great honour for me.” Appointed in August, the Spaniard said he was beginning to understand the nature of the rivalry with Germany. “Now I can understand more because I’m here and I feel this kind of rivalry. It will be a really good test for us,” Xavi said. In his press conference, Xavi deflected Klopp’s praise and said the Netherlands’ big win over Greece was down to his players. “It’s not Xavi-football. It’s all about the players. They are the most important. I don’t need to convince them to play this style of football, they have the capacity to play like the last game. Germany and the Netherlands played out a 1-1 draw in Amsterdam in September, the first match in charge for both Klopp and Xavi. Xavi said he would try and do the unexpected on Monday, but acknowledged it would not be easy against the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach. “It’s difficult to surprise a coach like Jurgen Klopp,” Xavi said. “He’s one of the best coaches in the past few years. And it’s an honour to come up against him tomorrow.” Vanguard News The post ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: Nets Crumble Without Porter Jr. As Grizzlies Dominate
top.description: Matthew Smith-Imagn Images The Brooklyn Nets fell apart after their top scorer was ruled out before tipoff for personal reasons. They lost 129-110 to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night at FedEx Forum before a crowd of 15,103 fans. Michael Porter Jr. was Brooklyn’s leading scorer, but he played in his uniform, not street clothes. Brooklyn coach Jordi Fernández explained the late timing of the news. He said, “No, not yet. A personal situation came up as we were coming to the arena. So that’s why it was announced late.” Fernández added that the team still lacks details on when Porter might return. “We don’t have any more information right now,” he told the press. Porter was listed as questionable earlier in the day before the team ruled him out an hour before tipoff. Cam Spencer sank a three-pointer to push the score to 35-17 with only 2:47 remaining in the first quarter. The Grizzlies built a massive lead that Brooklyn could not close even when Julius Randle hit a shot. Despite securing a team-leading 22 points and five assists, Randle had trouble on the glass, managing only four rebounds. He was also a minus-18, showing how much the team struggled without their main scoring option. Day’Ron Sharpe posted a double-double. He recorded 16 points, 11 rebounds, and five assists in the losing effort. Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. also returned to action after missing time due to illness. He played 19 minutes but could not change the outcome of the game. Memphis controlled the pace without their own leading scorer, Ty Jerome. Cedrick Coward scored a game-high 23 points for the Grizzlies. Taylor Hendricks added 22 points and helped seal the victory with a dunk that put Memphis up 101-78 late in the third quarter. The Nets gave up a 16-1 run. The team fell behind by 26 points after a three-pointer by Javon Small with 7:08 left to play. Porter leads the Nets in scoring with 21.5 points per game this season. He has been a key part of the offense alongside Randle, helping the team run more efficient plays. The team had shifted away from too many isolation plays to use more dynamic offense with Porter and Sharpe. The loss marks a rough end to a four-game road trip for the Brooklyn franchise.

top.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of prioritising campaign propaganda and political patronage over funding critical sectors of the economy, alleging that the huge spending on political publicity explains the poor implementation of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 budgets. The opposition party challenged the Federal Government to publish verifiable figures showing how much had been released for critical capital projects and administrative subventions in the three fiscal years, compared with expenditure on political advertisements and patronage. The NDC made the allegations in a statement signed on Sunday by the Spokesperson of its National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu, titled, “Dear Mr. President: The Huge Cost of Your Campaign Propaganda Testifies to Why You Failed to Adequately Fund 2024, 2025 and 2026 Budgets.” The party said its assessment of what it described as a barrage of political advertisements, donations, vehicles, laptops, sewing machines, food items and other gifts distributed by groups and individuals claiming to support Tinubu had raised questions about the administration’s spending priorities. It alleged that despite increased government revenue following the removal of fuel subsidy and higher taxation, critical social and physical infrastructure, national security and citizens’ welfare had not received adequate funding. Ikokwu said: “For instance, despite the palpable insecurity confronting the nation, only about seven per cent of the Defence Capital Budget was reportedly released in 2025. “Even more disturbing was when the Minister of Health reported that only ₦36 million out of the ₦218 billion allocated to Health Capital expenditure was released in the same 2025.” The party argued that the alleged low releases for defence and health raised questions about the government’s commitment to addressing insecurity and improving public services. It also expressed concern over the implementation of the 2026 budget, which it claimed had received inadequate attention, and accused the APC of devoting substantial resources to campaign publicity and political patronage ahead of the 2027 elections. Questioning the administration’s spending priorities, Ikokwu asked how a government benefiting from fuel subsidy removal and increased taxation could plead a lack of funds for national security, healthcare, education, federal roads and the welfare of ordinary Nigerians while political activities appeared to attract substantial resources. top.title: No. 1 South Carolina holds off JuJu Watkins’ No. 3 USC
top.description: GREENVILLE, S.C. — Not six minutes into an event dubbed “The Real SC” — after all, why go with something as simple as “No. 1 South Carolina versus No. 3 USC” when you can pretend the stakes are existential — things got real feisty. The ball found its way into the hands of Gamecocks forward Chloe Kitts. JuJu Watkins swarmed for the Trojans. Watkins and Kitts yanked and fought past the whistle for a jump ball. The USC star then brushed by Kitts as she walked away, spiking the volume in Bon Secours Arena, which included her front-row fan club featuring Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. One mid-November game won’t define the teams in it, but it can say something about the order of priority from there. Sunday was an opportunity for USC, in pursuit of its first national title in more than 40 years, to venture into hostility and assert itself in that territory. But an 89-85 win for the Gamecocks was, in the end, a product of players who have been there and done that doing it once again. The veteran trio of Tessa Johnson, Joyce Edwards and Kitts combined for 63 points and junior Jordan Lee hustled back for a block on a shot from Watkins that could’ve tied the game with 15.6 seconds left. USC’s stars struggled with efficiency for the better part of the afternoon, with sophomore Jazzy Davidson and freshman Saniyah Hall in particular showing their youth in moments. Then they demonstrated how dangerous they can be at the very end, nearly overcoming an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. Watkins, a national player of the year favorite, scored 11 of her 25 points in the final frame. This story will be updated. This article originally appeared in The Athletic . top.title: Weather is usually great at Charles Schwab but these 2 elements present a challenge
top.description: PHOENIX — Like pro golf in other places this time of year, shorter days and earlier sunsets add a little something to the mix. At the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, long shadows late in the day throw shade on many of the holes on the second nine at Phoenix Country Club. The field is just 36 qualifiers for this PGA Tour Champions season finale but the first tee time isn't until 10:25 a.m. local, with the final pairing heading out at 1:05 p.m. local. Sunset this time of year is right around 5:30 p.m., and with the senior golfers, who play in twosomes, usually moving at a pretty good clip, it's not a matter of running out of daylight. But the tall trees on the property cast some long shadows on the narrow corridors and greens late in the day on this parkland-style layout. Those shadows appear to be quite pronounced on TV during Golf Channel's coverage but for the players, it's just another thing they deal with. "It doesn't really affect it that much because it's not like you're, I mean, we've played here. With the exception of Zach [Johnson, a first-timer in this event], most have played here some," said first-round leader Stewart Cink, who had eight straight pars on Nos. 8 through 15 before closing with birdies on 16 and 18. "You kind of know what the ball's going to do on the greens. You're not just like learning for the first time in the shadows." Another element, at least on the par-4 12th and the par-4 14th, is the late-afternoon ball of fire in the sky. "I thought the difficult part was a lot of these holes just go directly into the setting sun and as the afternoon wore on, there was a lot of shots where you had a hard time picking out the flag because the sun was sinking low," Cink said. "Everybody has to deal with that a little bit, it's not a big factor, but it definitely was something noticeable." Todd Kelly is Golfweek's assistant managing editor . top.title: Michael Kim explains why Rory McIlroy had a ‘big advantage’ over Eugenio Chacarra in Race to Dubai battle
top.description: Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images Rory McIlroy produced a late comeback to overtake Eugenio Chacarra in the Race to Dubai standings on the final day of the DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy’s solo second-place finish was enough to secure the season-long title, despite Chacarra also enjoying an impressive week with a tied-third finish. Tyrrell Hatton claimed victory in Dubai, but the biggest prize went to McIlroy, who has now won a record-equalling eight Race to Dubai titles alongside Colin Montgomerie. PGA Tour player Michael Kim has since explained why the Northern Irishman held a significant advantage over Chacarra throughout the season. Michael Kim reveals Rory McIlroy’s key advantage over Eugenio Chacarra Michael Kim believes Rory McIlroy had a significant advantage over Eugenio Chacarra in the Race to Dubai battle because of the way points are distributed across the DP World Tour season. He pointed to the weighting given to major championships as a key factor in the 37-year-old’s success. “Rory had a big advantage, with the points very far skewed toward the majors. Eugenio played awesome this year to even give himself a shot at the Race to Dubai,” Kim tweeted. McIlroy’s major championship performances proved crucial, as he won the Masters and finished tied seventh at the PGA Championship. top.title: U.S. women's hockey team gets Canada in world championship final with historic streak at stake
top.description: The U.S. and Canada will meet in the World Women's Hockey Championship final for the 24th time in 25 all-time editions. This time, the U.S. is carrying its longest winning streak in major international competition. The reigning Olympic and world champion beat Finland 5-0 in the semifinals on Sunday in Denmark. Later, Canada won 3-0 over Sweden, which made its first world semi since 2009. The Americans are 6-0 at these worlds, winning every game by at least five goals. Since the start of the 2025 Worlds, the U.S. has won 20 consecutive games between World Championship and Olympic play, a program record. On Sunday, captain Hilary Knight led the way with one goal and one assist, while Aerin Frankel stopped all 13 Finland shots. Earlier in the tournament, the U.S. broke the record for most shots in a single women's worlds game, registering 85 in a 14-0 quarterfinal win over Denmark on Friday. The U.S. had the previous record of 82 from 1997. The 14 goals marked the most for the U.S. in a worlds game since 2000. Frankel broke the American goalie record for most career game wins in worlds history. Frankel is now up to 20 victories, bettering Jessie Vetter's old record of 16. Caroline Harvey broke the record for most career points in world championship play for a U.S. defender, even though she is still just 24 years old. Knight, playing in her 16th worlds at age 37, leads the tournament with seven goals in six games, while Harvey has the most points (15) and Taylor Fox (née Heise) has the most assists (12). Canada is playing a major tournament without Marie-Philip Poulin for the first time since 2008. Poulin had surgery in July for a torn ACL and meniscus. Caroline Harvey willed herself to become one of the world’s best hockey players Caroline Harvey trained at a famous boxing gym before becoming an Olympic hockey player as a teenager. Nick Zaccardi ,

nigeria.title: NDC candidate in Kwara pledges N120,000 minimum wage for workers
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kwara, Prof. Abdulmumin Ajia, has pledged a minimum wage of N120,000 for workers in the state. Ajia made the pledge on Sunday in Ilorin while unveiling the NDC’s 2027 Gubernatorial Campaign Council manifesto, tagged ‘Forward Kwara Agenda’. He proposed a N120,000 public-service minimum wage benchmark and a cost-of-living adjustment framework for workers and pensioners. He said his administration would verify the payroll, assess the financial implications, consult labour unions and publish an implementation and funding timetable. On pensioners, Ajia promised to verify outstanding gratuities and publish a schedule for settling validated arrears. He also pledged to establish a predictable payment timetable for newly due pension obligations. Ajia said he entered the governorship race to make public institutions work reliably for all Kwarans, regardless of political affiliation. “I am running to make public institutions work that way. If entrusted with office, I will serve people who support me, people who oppose me and people who have never attended a political meeting,” he said. He said his experience as a teacher, researcher and university administrator had taught him to ask critical questions, examine evidence and take responsibility for results. Ajia, who led a School of Business and mentored young people, said his visits home exposed him to the challenges facing unemployed graduates. He said many young people could hardly predict when fair employment opportunities would become available. According to him, government has a responsibility to ensure that citizens understand how to access assistance, eligibility requirements and appeal procedures. He said access to public services should not depend on personal relationships with the governor. Ajia said the Forward Kwara Agenda outlined six areas of governance, anchored on stronger institutions, greater opportunities and shared prosperity. On security, he said farmers should access their farms, children should travel safely to school and traders should return home safely from markets. nigeria.title: ‘Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football’ – Klopp praises Netherlands coach
nigeria.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp praised Xavi Hernandez on Sunday, saying the new Netherlands coach already had the Dutch playing in his own image after just five games in charge. Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday’s meeting between the two old rivals, Klopp pointed to Friday’s 7-0 thumping of Greece in Amsterdam and said the former midfielder had made an impression. Considered among the best midfielders in the history of the game, Xavi formed the core of a possession-dominant Barcelona side who won four Champions League titles. He also won the World Cup with Spain. “They simply played some electric football,” Klopp said, adding: “Xavi wants to play Xavi-style football… “He’s a coach who really pushes his approach to the limit. And that’s exciting. I always loved playing against teams who play like this.” Third in the group with only the top two reaching the quarter-finals, Germany will need to beat the Netherlands to give themselves a chance. “They’re a team who really come alive in European football,” Klopp said of the Netherlands. “It’s one of the fiercest rivalries in football. It’s a great honour for me.” Appointed in August, the Spaniard said he was beginning to understand the nature of the rivalry with Germany. “Now I can understand more because I’m here and I feel this kind of rivalry. It will be a really good test for us,” Xavi said. In his press conference, Xavi deflected Klopp’s praise and said the Netherlands’ big win over Greece was down to his players. “It’s not Xavi-football. It’s all about the players. They are the most important. I don’t need to convince them to play this style of football, they have the capacity to play like the last game. Germany and the Netherlands played out a 1-1 draw in Amsterdam in September, the first match in charge for both Klopp and Xavi. Xavi said he would try and do the unexpected on Monday, but acknowledged it would not be easy against the former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach. “It’s difficult to surprise a coach like Jurgen Klopp,” Xavi said. “He’s one of the best coaches in the past few years. A trailer with an unknown registration number was seen overturned on its side, with its container crushed and contents scattered across the road, while other trailers were rammed into one another behind it. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. sports.title: Nets Crumble Without Porter Jr. As Grizzlies Dominate
sports.description: Matthew Smith-Imagn Images The Brooklyn Nets fell apart after their top scorer was ruled out before tipoff for personal reasons. They lost 129-110 to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday night at FedEx Forum before a crowd of 15,103 fans. Michael Porter Jr. was Brooklyn’s leading scorer, but he played in his uniform, not street clothes. Brooklyn coach Jordi Fernández explained the late timing of the news. He said, “No, not yet. A personal situation came up as we were coming to the arena. So that’s why it was announced late.” Fernández added that the team still lacks details on when Porter might return. “We don’t have any more information right now,” he told the press. Porter was listed as questionable earlier in the day before the team ruled him out an hour before tipoff. Cam Spencer sank a three-pointer to push the score to 35-17 with only 2:47 remaining in the first quarter. The Grizzlies built a massive lead that Brooklyn could not close even when Julius Randle hit a shot. Despite securing a team-leading 22 points and five assists, Randle had trouble on the glass, managing only four rebounds. He was also a minus-18, showing how much the team struggled without their main scoring option. Day’Ron Sharpe posted a double-double. He recorded 16 points, 11 rebounds, and five assists in the losing effort. Rookie Mikel Brown Jr. also returned to action after missing time due to illness. He played 19 minutes but could not change the outcome of the game. Memphis controlled the pace without their own leading scorer, Ty Jerome. Cedrick Coward scored a game-high 23 points for the Grizzlies. Taylor Hendricks added 22 points and helped seal the victory with a dunk that put Memphis up 101-78 late in the third quarter. The Nets gave up a 16-1 run. The team fell behind by 26 points after a three-pointer by Javon Small with 7:08 left to play. Porter leads the Nets in scoring with 21.5 points per game this season. He has been a key part of the offense alongside Randle, helping the team run more efficient plays. The team had shifted away from too many isolation plays to use more dynamic offense with Porter and Sharpe. The loss marks a rough end to a four-game road trip for the Brooklyn franchise.

sports.title: No. 1 South Carolina holds off JuJu Watkins’ No. 3 USC
sports.description: GREENVILLE, S.C. — Not six minutes into an event dubbed “The Real SC” — after all, why go with something as simple as “No. 1 South Carolina versus No. 3 USC” when you can pretend the stakes are existential — things got real feisty. The ball found its way into the hands of Gamecocks forward Chloe Kitts. JuJu Watkins swarmed for the Trojans. Watkins and Kitts yanked and fought past the whistle for a jump ball. The USC star then brushed by Kitts as she walked away, spiking the volume in Bon Secours Arena, which included her front-row fan club featuring Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. One mid-November game won’t define the teams in it, but it can say something about the order of priority from there. Sunday was an opportunity for USC, in pursuit of its first national title in more than 40 years, to venture into hostility and assert itself in that territory. But an 89-85 win for the Gamecocks was, in the end, a product of players who have been there and done that doing it once again. The veteran trio of Tessa Johnson, Joyce Edwards and Kitts combined for 63 points and junior Jordan Lee hustled back for a block on a shot from Watkins that could’ve tied the game with 15.6 seconds left. USC’s stars struggled with efficiency for the better part of the afternoon, with sophomore Jazzy Davidson and freshman Saniyah Hall in particular showing their youth in moments. Then they demonstrated how dangerous they can be at the very end, nearly overcoming an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. sports.title: Weather is usually great at Charles Schwab but these 2 elements present a challenge
sports.description: PHOENIX — Like pro golf in other places this time of year, shorter days and earlier sunsets add a little something to the mix. At the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, long shadows late in the day throw shade on many of the holes on the second nine at Phoenix Country Club. The field is just 36 qualifiers for this PGA Tour Champions season finale but the first tee time isn't until 10:25 a.m. local, with the final pairing heading out at 1:05 p.m. local. Sunset this time of year is right around 5:30 p.m., and with the senior golfers, who play in twosomes, usually moving at a pretty good clip, it's not a matter of running out of daylight. But the tall trees on the property cast some long shadows on the narrow corridors and greens late in the day on this parkland-style layout. Those shadows appear to be quite pronounced on TV during Golf Channel's coverage but for the players, it's just another thing they deal with. "It doesn't really affect it that much because it's not like you're, I mean, we've played here. With the exception of Zach [Johnson, a first-timer in this event], most have played here some," said first-round leader Stewart Cink, who had eight straight pars on Nos. 8 through 15 before closing with birdies on 16 and 18. "You kind of know what the ball's going to do on the greens. You're not just like learning for the first time in the shadows." Another element, at least on the par-4 12th and the par-4 14th, is the late-afternoon ball of fire in the sky. "I thought the difficult part was a lot of these holes just go directly into the setting sun and as the afternoon wore on, there was a lot of shots where you had a hard time picking out the flag because the sun was sinking low," Cink said. "Everybody has to deal with that a little bit, it's not a big factor, but it definitely was something noticeable." Todd Kelly is Golfweek's assistant managing editor . sports.title: Michael Kim explains why Rory McIlroy had a ‘big advantage’ over Eugenio Chacarra in Race to Dubai battle
sports.description: Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images Rory McIlroy produced a late comeback to overtake Eugenio Chacarra in the Race to Dubai standings on the final day of the DP World Tour Championship. McIlroy’s solo second-place finish was enough to secure the season-long title, despite Chacarra also enjoying an impressive week with a tied-third finish. Tyrrell Hatton claimed victory in Dubai, but the biggest prize went to McIlroy, who has now won a record-equalling eight Race to Dubai titles alongside Colin Montgomerie. PGA Tour player Michael Kim has since explained why the Northern Irishman held a significant advantage over Chacarra throughout the season. Michael Kim reveals Rory McIlroy’s key advantage over Eugenio Chacarra Michael Kim believes Rory McIlroy had a significant advantage over Eugenio Chacarra in the Race to Dubai battle because of the way points are distributed across the DP World Tour season. He pointed to the weighting given to major championships as a key factor in the 37-year-old’s success. “Rory had a big advantage, with the points very far skewed toward the majors. Eugenio played awesome this year to even give himself a shot at the Race to Dubai,” Kim tweeted. McIlroy’s major championship performances proved crucial, as he won the Masters and finished tied seventh at the PGA Championship. He also recorded top-40 finishes at both the US Open and The Open, while Chacarra featured in just one major, finishing tied-46th at Royal Birkdale. The Spaniard enjoyed an excellent season on the DP World Tour , winning the Italian Open, Dutch Open and India Championship. He also finished tied-22nd in Abu Dhabi and third in Dubai, but those results were not enough to overhaul McIlroy. sports.title: Week 11 Report Card: Exemplary grades for Oregon after Michigan win
sports.description: When the Oregon Ducks came in at No. 16 in the College Football Playoff rankings this week, the possibility of earning an at-large bid to the 12-team field appeared to be on the table. While the three losses that the Ducks have on their resume isn't ideal, they've played like a playoff team the two previous weeks. That needed to continue in the final three regular season games for the Playoff Committee to even be able to consider placing Oregon in the CFP. Game one of three, coming against the Michigan Wolverines , check. Oregon looked about as impressive as they could've hoped on Saturday, putting the locks on Michigan's offense in allowing just a single touchdown in the 31-7 convincing win. The 31 points (four touchdowns, one field goal) was the most that the Wolverines have allowed all season long — by a whopping ten points. At times, the Ducks looked like a far more physical team than the Wolverines, widely-regarded for their physicality and toughness. If the Playoff Committee isn't impressed with a win in which nearly every positon group for the Ducks excelled, I'm not sure what else they could do. Let's get into this week's report card, where it's difficult to find much criticism and easy to find a lot of praise after the 23-point victory. Quarterbacks Grade: A There was only one definite throw that Dylan Raiola made in which he put the ball in serious harms way. But other than that, Raiola was nails and put forth his best performance as the Ducks' starter this season. He was precise and on fire from the very beginning, finishing the first quarter going 8-for-8 for 133 yards and two touchdowns, one being a 60-yard moon ball to Jeremiah McClellan. The next drive, he floated a pass to Evan Stewart for another big gain. Raiola has been on the field a lot in 2026, and this was the best version. Running Backs Grade: A- With Jordon Davison still out injured, it was up to Dierre Hill Jr. to take a bulk of the carries out of the backfield. In toting the rock 21 times, Hill churned out 98 yards including a long of 36 yards. Each of Hill's best skills were on display, as he was dynamic with the football on each touch. He caught a swing pass in the fourth quarter and weaved his way for a 49-yard touchdown, putting the Wolverines out of their misery. True freshman Brandon Smith also recorded 29 rushing yards on seven carries while Da'Jaun Riggs caught a short touchdown out of the backfield. His 60-yard touchdown on the opening drive affirmed that he was back to full strength, as he ran past multiple Wolverines despite being held. Dakorien Moore was his usual reliable self, catching seven passes for 88 yards and a score — though he did drop a would-be touchdown in the end zone, leading to the A- grade. sports.title: On Keeping Crosby, Malkin Together: ‘The Option’s There’
sports.description: Pittsburgh Penguins coach Dan Muse had the perfect opening to make tweaks – or even tsunamis – to his personnel on Sunday. The team doesn’t play again until Thursday and was coming off a frustrating 4-1 loss to Ottawa. Instead, Muse held course, with the lines , defensive pairs and power-play units the same during practice at the UPMC Lemieux Sports Complex. That meant that the top line still sported Evgeni Malkin , Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell . Long-time teammates and future Hall of Famers Malkin, 40, and Crosby, 39, have played together at times over the years. Early on, sometimes they would last on the same line for a few games. In recent years, it’s been more of a situational thing – thrown together after a penalty kill or for a few shifts to try to spark some offense. But it’s been four games now with that top line. The return of injured winger Bryan Rust could provide a reason to break up that trio, but his return is not imminent – he and forward Elmer Soderblom continue to skate before practice. So could Crosby and Malkin remain together for a while this time? “Yeah, I think so,” Penguins coach Dan Muse said. “Every year’s different. With that and everything else, sometimes you make changes over the course of the year. It’s something that we wanted to see. I know that they do have time together in the past, so there’s some familiarity there. I think the option’s there for sure.” Of course, with the way the lines have been shuffled as the Penguins seek consistency and balance, the coaches could just as well break up that line by practice Monday. One facilitating factor for keeping it intact is Malkin’s move from center to wing last season. Previously, placing him on Crosby’s line diluted the team’s strength down the middle, and so was nearly always considered a temporary solution to a sagging offense. It could also be pointed out that with those two veterans – three if you include Rakell – together, it potentially opens up more room for younger players on the other lines. So in a season that seems to be stuck in the mud , why not keep them together for the foreseeable future? The guy who makes up the third portion of the line, Rakell, is convinced it could work. “Yeah, I think so. We’re very familiar with everybody’s game and tendencies on the ice,” he said. “Just trying to work off each other. We can make things happen off the rush. But also when we’re all going, we’re very comfortable being on the forecheck and scoring on rebounds. “I think we can get better and better, and try to lead the way for the team.” In their four games since the line was formed, Crosby has a two goals and an assist, Malkin has six assists, and Rakell has a goal and an assist. While they had no points and seemed quiet in the game Saturday against Ottawa, their metrics as a line combination are good, including a 75.00 GF%, 71.43 HDCF% and 62.10 Corsi For. Muse smiled when asked about their advanced stats and the impact that might have on keeping them together.

sports.title: Louisville embarrassed at Memphis, 98-78
sports.description: FAYETTEVILLE, ARKANSAS - OCTOBER 28: Head Coach Penny Hardaway of the Memphis Tigers signals to the bench during a game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Bud Walton Arena on October 28, 2026 in Fayetteville, Arkansas. The Razorbacks defeated the Tigers 93-81. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images For a season that was supposed to be different in all the right ways, Sunday felt an awful lot like the same song and dance Louisville fans have seen from previous Pat Kelsey teams in big spots on the road. U of L led by as many as 18 points in the first half and by 11 at halftime, but was destroyed in the second half by unranked Memphis, who rolled to a 98-78 victory over their longtime rivals to the North. The comeback was the fourth-largest in the last 15 years by an unranked team against an AP top 10 opponent. The Tigers shot over 70 percent from the field in the second half and out-scored their visitors 57-26 after the break. Point guard Jayden Reid led the way with 24 points and 10 assists, while Tylik Weeks added 24 points of his own, 18 of those coming in the second half. Seth Trimble seemed to be the only Cardinal not rattled during the second half avalanche. The transfer from North Carolina scored 16 points and added two steals and two blocks. Jackson Shelstad scored 16 as well, but had just one made basket after halftime. Look, there’s no way to sugarcoat it: This was a very very, VERY bad way to, in earnest, begin what we all agree is pretty much a defining season for Pat Kelsey at Louisville. In a major spot, the Cards were once again the less composed, less tough, and less hungry team. That can’t happen when we’re talking about one of the 5-10 highest-paid rosters in the sport and a team that many experts believe should be a Final Four contender. You went all in last spring on being one of the best defensive teams in the country, and you just gave up 98 to a Memphis team playing without its second-leading scorer. This team needs to be elite defensively to have any shot whatsoever at being great overall. Sunday, it wasn’t even average defensively. I know it’s November, but these three games coming up in Las Vegas on Thanksgiving Week could not be more important.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? science.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
science.description: null For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab) "The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold." Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event. "There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the Goddard Spaceflight Center , told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption." science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment. A look at the 33 Raptor engines of Starship's Super Heavy booster during the vehicle's Flight 15 test launch on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Josh Dinner, Space.com/Future) Rocket recovery is only part of the reuse equation, of course; there's also refurbishment and reflight. And that gets us back to the "work left to do" discussion, for SpaceX has yet to demonstrate rapid reflight with either Super Heavy or Ship. science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. science.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
science.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO.
